about.title: About the researcher
about.intro: I'm Yeonoh Park (박연오), a Computer Engineering undergraduate at Seoul National University of Science and Technology (SeoulTech) and an undergraduate researcher at the Cryptography Information Security Laboratory.
about.focus: I study how identity, authority, and trust move across software boundaries, and whether software enforces the security boundaries it is intended to provide.

roles.label: TCP · Computer Science and Information Technology Club

research.title: Research in numbers
research.scope: Authorization boundaries, tenant isolation, credential handling, workflow execution, plugins, and APIs across open-source projects and coordinated disclosure programs.
research.note: The 92 reports were submitted from March 22 to August 13, 2026. The 13 vendor-confirmed outcomes include subsequent confirmations and publications.

steps.label: Model the boundary
steps.detail: Identify the identities, capabilities, data domains, and trust transitions that define a system's expected security properties.

steps.label: Follow authority
steps.detail: Trace how identity and scope propagate between components, looking for changes in how authority is interpreted.

steps.label: Check the evidence
steps.detail: Use bounded local validation and competing explanations to distinguish a boundary failure from expected behavior.

steps.label: Coordinate disclosure
steps.detail: Separate technical impact from reportability, account for prior work, document limitations, and work with vendors on disclosure.
